biography.plain_text: Raymond L. Lutgert was an American property developer who built a real estate business in Chicago before creating Park Shore in Naples, Florida. He had worked in his father's building materials yard before developing homes and shopping centres. The privately held Lutgert Companies expanded into waterfront apartments and golf communities.

long_biography.plain_text:
Raymond L. Lutgert's sculptures became public landmarks alongside the Naples developments that made his name. He began studying sculpture at Appalachian State University when he was 65 and went on to produce hundreds of works. Working in stone and metal, he created pieces for courtyards, shopping streets and college campuses.

At The Village on Venetian Bay, his work ranges from the fountain sculpture Water Nymph to Human Race, a group of rising stainless-steel columns. Raymond and his wife Beverly also helped finance Florida Gulf Coast University's business college building through a joint gift that attracted matching state funds. The university displays another version of Human Race beside Lutgert Hall.
